duplicates_suppressed.finding: Hardcoded store name in report header

findings.title: InwardScreen stock check failure allows 'Submit Anyway' bypass to submit unverified stock
findings.description: When the pre-submission stock level check API call fails (network error, timeout, server error), the catch block presents an Alert with a 'Submit Anyway' button that calls doSubmit() directly, bypassing stock verification entirely. This means a retailer on a flaky connection can submit stock inward transactions without the server ever validating current levels, potentially creating phantom inventory or double-counting stock.
findings.impact: Stock inward transactions can be submitted without verification, leading to incorrect inventory counts. In production, unreliable network conditions could make this the common path rather than the exception.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'Submit Anyway' option. When stock check fails, only offer 'Cancel' and 'Retry'. If retries also fail, queue the transaction for offline sync (using offlineQueue) so it can be verified when back online.

findings.title: SuccessPrintScreenV2 uses setTimeout(0) for cart unlock after navigation.reset creating a race condition
findings.description: After a sale completes and the user taps 'No Print' (handleSkip), the code calls navigation.reset() to go back to SellScan and then setTimeout(() => unlockCart(), 0) to unlock the cart. The setTimeout(0) relies on the assumption that React Navigation processes reset synchronously before the next microtask tick. If navigation takes longer (e.g., during heavy rendering or on slow devices), the cart could unlock before SellScan mounts, or SellScan could briefly render with a locked cart. Additionally, if the component unmounts before setTimeout fires, the unlockCart call could be lost entirely.
findings.impact: On slow devices or during heavy rendering, the cart may remain locked after returning to SellScan, preventing the user from starting a new sale. Requires app restart to recover.
findings.recommendation: Use React Navigation's navigation state listener or beforeRemove event to trigger unlockCart when SellScan actually mounts, rather than relying on setTimeout timing. Alternatively, have SellScan's useEffect check and unlock the cart on mount as a safety net.

findings.title: ReorderSettingsScreen displays autoApproveThreshold as raw number without formatMoney
findings.description: The auto-approve threshold value is displayed as {settings?.autoApproveThreshold} directly in a <Text> component without passing it through formatMoney(). If the backend stores this value in minor units (paise), the user would see '50000' instead of the formatted currency '500.00' or a properly formatted INR display. Even if stored in major units, the display lacks currency symbol and grouping.
findings.impact: Users see a confusing raw number for the threshold (e.g., '50000' vs '₹500.00'), making the setting hard to understand and potentially leading to misconfigured auto-approval thresholds.
findings.recommendation: Use formatMoney(settings.autoApproveThreshold) to display the value. Determine if the value is in minor or major units and convert accordingly.

findings.title: ReorderSettingsScreen autoApproveThreshold null check allows undefined to show empty row
findings.description: The condition {settings?.autoApproveThreshold !== null && (...)} only checks for null, not undefined. If the API returns the field as undefined (omitted from response), the expression evaluates to true (since undefined !== null), causing the row to render with an empty value display.
findings.impact: An empty 'Auto-Approve Threshold' row could appear with no value when the setting hasn't been configured, confusing users.
findings.recommendation: Change the condition to {settings?.autoApproveThreshold != null && (...)} (loose equality) to catch both null and undefined, or use a more explicit check like {typeof settings?.autoApproveThreshold === 'number' && (...)}.

findings.title: OrderDetailScreen WhatsApp button opens wa.me without supplier phone number
findings.description: The handleWhatsAppSupplier function opens https://wa.me/?text=... without including a phone number in the URL. The code comments acknowledge 'supplierPhone not available on PurchaseOrder type'. This forces the user to manually select the supplier from their WhatsApp contact list, defeating the purpose of a quick-action button. The supplier phone should either be included in the PurchaseOrder API response or fetched separately.
findings.code_snippet:
// supplierPhone not available on PurchaseOrder type — open wa.me without phone so user picks contact
const url = `https://wa.me/?text=${message}`;
findings.impact: Every time a retailer taps the WhatsApp button on an order, they must manually find and select the supplier contact. This adds friction to what should be a one-tap action, reducing adoption of the feature.
findings.recommendation: Include supplier phone number in the PurchaseOrderWithItems API response. Update the URL to https://wa.me/{supplierPhone}?text={message}. If phone is unavailable, show a toast explaining why manual selection is needed.

findings.title: StockStatementScreen uses 'as any' type assertions to call stock status helpers
findings.description: The StockCard component casts item.stockStatus (typed as string) to any before passing it to getStockStatusColor() and getStockStatusLabel(). This bypasses TypeScript's type safety and could lead to runtime errors if the API returns unexpected stock status values that the helper functions don't handle.
findings.code_snippet:
const statusColor = getStockStatusColor(item.stockStatus as any);
const statusLabel = getStockStatusLabel(item.stockStatus as any);
findings.impact: If the API returns a stock status value not handled by the helper functions (e.g., a new status added on the backend), the component could render undefined colors or labels with no compile-time warning.
findings.recommendation: Update the StockItem interface to use the proper stock status union type that getStockStatusColor/getStockStatusLabel expect, eliminating the need for 'as any' casts.

findings.title: SellScanScreen error status check uses unsafe type assertion instead of ApiError instanceof
findings.description: In the handleEditProductSave catch block, after calling asError(_e), the code checks for 409 status using (e as { status?: number }).status. This is an unsafe type assertion. The error is already typed as Error after asError(), and the proper pattern (used elsewhere like PaymentSetupScreen) is to check `e instanceof ApiError` which has a typed status property.
findings.impact: The type assertion could mask issues where the status property doesn't exist on the error object. While functionally equivalent (status would be undefined, not 409), it breaks the type-safety convention used throughout the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Replace the unsafe cast with: if (e instanceof ApiError && e.status === 409) { ... }. This follows the same pattern used in PaymentSetupScreen and other screens.

findings.title: SuccessPrintScreenV2 hardcodes 'SuperMandi POS' in receipt text instead of dynamic store name
findings.description: The thermal receipt text generation in generateReceiptContent() hardcodes 'SuperMandi POS' as the header on line 87. The actual store name is available via the store session but is not used for the receipt header. Unlike R5.POS.068 which covers the DailyReportScreen report header, this is the customer-facing printed receipt — the most visible branding surface for the retailer.
findings.impact: Every printed receipt shows 'SuperMandi POS' instead of the actual store name. Retailers who white-label or want their own store name on receipts cannot customize this. Customer-facing receipts should show the store's actual business name.
findings.recommendation: Fetch the store name from device session (e.g., from the same source as operatorStoreId) and use formatStoreName() to display it in the receipt header. Fall back to 'SuperMandi POS' only if store name is unavailable.

findings.title: Multiple screens missing i18n (useTranslation) with all-English hardcoded strings
findings.description: At least 6 screens do not import useTranslation from react-i18next and have all user-facing text hardcoded in English. The app supports Hindi via i18n, but these screens will always display in English regardless of the user's language setting. Other screens in the same feature area (e.g., ReorderSettingsScreen) do use useTranslation, creating an inconsistent experience when switching between screens in Hindi mode.
findings.impact: Hindi-speaking users see a jarring mix of Hindi and English when navigating between screens. PaymentSetupScreen is particularly impactful since it's part of the onboarding flow where Hindi-speaking users are most likely to need native language support.
findings.recommendation: Add useTranslation() to all listed screens and extract all hardcoded strings to i18n translation keys. Prioritize PaymentSetupScreen (onboarding flow) and OrderDetailScreen (frequent use).

findings.title: OrderDetailScreen auto-refresh polls every 30s indefinitely for non-final orders with no max attempts
findings.description: The useEffect on line 116-131 sets up a 30-second polling interval for order status updates when the order is not in a final state (delivered/cancelled). The polling has no maximum attempt limit, no backoff strategy, and no pause when the app is in the background. If a user leaves the OrderDetailScreen open (e.g., navigated to it but then switched apps), the polling continues indefinitely, consuming battery and network resources.
findings.impact: Battery drain and unnecessary network traffic when the screen is left open or app is backgrounded. On metered connections, this adds up to significant data usage over time. Note: R5.POS.060 covers a similar pattern in BnplDuesScreen but this is a different screen with different polling characteristics.
findings.recommendation: Add AppState listener to pause polling when app is backgrounded. Add a maximum attempt count (e.g., 60 attempts = 30 minutes). Consider using exponential backoff for orders that have been in the same status for a long time.
